_comment: Baseline of tests/engine-invariants.html. Each value hashes that configuration's rounded KPI set; open the harness and treat any changed fingerprint on an unchanged configuration as a regression. __all hashes the whole set.
_caveat: The hash covers the WHOLE KPI object, so ADDING an output key changes every fingerprint even though no number moved. A wholesale change across unrelated configurations usually means new KPI keys, not a regression. Confirm by extracting the previous engine (git show <prev>:src/calc.js), running both against the same inputs, and comparing only the keys that existed before. Re-baseline once that shows no drift.
_history: 860fe56 pre mixed-use. Mixed-use left all 34 fingerprints byte-identical. The debt-facility fix deliberately moved 29. Leasehold land added 5 KPI keys; a value-level diff confirmed zero freehold drift. Ground rent then moved to a monthly accrual, moving only the four leasehold fingerprints. Encumbered exit (leasehold NOI capitalised net of ground rent) added the annualRentAtExit key, re-hashing everything; a value-level diff over 300 numbers across 6 freehold configurations again confirmed zero drift, and leasehold exit values fell as intended. Ground rent was then found MISSING from totalCashCosts while present in grossCashflow - profit was overstated by the entire rent (83.2M vs 45.6M on a test scheme) while IRR was already correct, which is why it read as a high profit beside a modest return. Only the four leasehold fingerprints moved.
